definition.text: Binding to an actin filament, also known as F-actin, a helical filamentous polymer of globular G-actin subunits.
The process in which an actin filament is broken down into smaller filaments.

A region of a sarcomere that appears as a light band on each side of the Z disc, comprising a region of the sarcomere where thin (actin) filaments are not overlapped by thick (myosin) filaments; contains actin, troponin, and tropomyosin; each sarcomere includes half of an I band at each end.

The space external to the outermost structure of a cell. For cells without external protective or external encapsulating structures this refers to space outside of the plasma membrane. This term covers the host cell environment outside an intracellular parasite.
The contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.

A cellular structure that forms the internal framework of eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells. The cytoskeleton includes intermediate filaments, microfilaments, microtubules, the microtrabecular lattice, and other structures characterized by a polymeric filamentous nature and long-range order within the cell. The various elements of the cytoskeleton not only serve in the maintenance of cellular shape but also have roles in other cellular functions, including cellular movement, cell division, endocytosis, and movement of organelles.

Platelike region of a muscle sarcomere to which the plus ends of actin filaments are attached.
Disassembly of actin filaments by the removal of actin monomers from a filament.

A dynamic, proteinaceous framework within the nucleus of eukaryotic cells, composed of proteins and RNA, that provides structural support for chromatin organization, gene regulation, and nuclear processes.

A vesicle that is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane. Extracellular exosomes, also simply called exosomes, have a diameter of about 40-100 nm.
Assembly or disassembly of actin filaments by the addition or removal of actin monomers from a filament.
Binding to an actin subunit and promoting its dissociation from an actin filament by a local change in actin subunit conformation and orientation, and severing of filaments.
Binding to monomeric or multimeric forms of actin, including actin filaments.
Binding to a ubiquitin protein ligase enzyme, any of the E3 proteins.
Binding to an enzyme, a protein with catalytic activity.
Binding to a small monomeric GTPase.
Binding to a heavy chain of the dynein complex.
Binding to a ubiquitin-like protein conjugating enzyme such as ubiquitin conjugating enzyme.

primary_access.PMID:25910212: Accessible original article text plus exact wild-type and variant human actin-pair records inspected. The selected HTML-derived cache lacks the full Methods. primary_access.PMID:31515488: Selected full screen Methods and exact human CFL2–ACTB variant record inspected. Source-specific no-effect annotation is retained, rather than generalized across publications.
primary_access.PMID:32296183: Accessible original HuRI assay description and exact nine human target-pair records inspected. Repeated screen representations and assay validations are not treated as independent physiological replication.
primary_access.PMID:32814053: Normal primary abstract and exact source-linked human DYNC1H1/KLK6 yeast two-hybrid records inspected. Full original Methods/construct boundaries were not recovered; no endogenous encounter or motor role is claimed.
primary_access.PMID:33961781: Accessible original BioPlex assay description and exact two cell-context co-IP records inspected. Complex association is distinguished from direct binary binding or obligate heterodimer formation.
primary_access.PMID:35271311: Selected accessible original article text plus official interaction CSV and bait-library metadata inspected. ACTB/ACTG1 baits and the CFL2 protein group are resolved; individual CFL2 isoforms are not separately assigned.
primary_access.PMID:35440100: Genuine full normal text inspected at selected structural Results, Figure 4 legend and expression/TIRF Methods. Full-length human CFL2 and rabbit skeletal actin are distinguished; TIRF tags were cleaved and left an extra N-terminal glycine. No figure-pixel inspection is claimed.
primary_access.PMID:25373779: Genuine full normal primary text selected for the independent mechanism peer. Purified-protein and cardiomyocyte/ortholog scope is distinguished from a new human developmental annotation.

bounded_peer.scope: Human direct severing/depolymerization, human muscle localization and patient/rat construct limits. No whole-source claim beyond the specified selected reads.

mechanistic_limits: Human full-length CFL2 has direct single-filament severing activity. NMR assembly explicitly uses rabbit skeletal actin; TIRF preparation and its tag cleavage are described separately.
The older human GST-CFL2 assay measures bulk depolymerization; its kit actin species was not specified.
The A35T patient phenotype and bacterial solubility experiment do not measure mutant depolymerization kinetics.
Human quadriceps Z-disc localization and neonatal rat cardiomyocyte pointed-end localization are distinct contexts; residence is not asserted to be universal or exclusive.

No NEW process or new annotation is proposed. The three machine-sourced alternative products remain unchanged; CFL1/CFL2 comparisons are paralog comparisons, not evidence that every CFL2 splice product was tested.

unresolved.reason: The genuine full primary text describes the human ORFeome yeast two-hybrid screen, but the exact CFL2–CFL1 entry lies in Supplementary Table 2, which was not recovered after bounded attempts. The current IntAct query yielded no matching source pair; absence from that query is not negative biological evidence. Preserve the original IPI assertion without claiming that a different publication verifies this particular experiment.

The genuine full primary text describes the human ORFeome yeast two-hybrid screen, but the exact CFL2–ACTB entry lies in Supplementary Table 2, which was not recovered after bounded attempts. The current IntAct query yielded no matching source pair; absence from that query is not negative biological evidence. Preserve the original IPI assertion without claiming that a different publication verifies this particular experiment.

The authentic abstract describes tear proteomics in untreated primary open-angle glaucoma and controls. Publisher supplementary files were identified but their actual CFL2 accession/peptide row could not be inspected; challenge and error responses were excluded. Preserve the HDA assertion rather than infer secretion, extracellular function or absence from a cytosolic protein annotation.

The original UniProt subcellular mapping is genuine and the selected UniProt record labels nuclear matrix by similarity. Current GO:0016363 denotes a specific nuclear protein/RNA framework; a nuclear-localization motif or broad nuclear actin-rod statement does not by itself resolve association with that framework. The historical donor experiment underlying this precise mapping was not reconstructed. This is an evidence-specific uncertainty, not a claim that CFL2 cannot enter the nucleus.

The genuine primary body describes LC-MS/MS of vesicles isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine, but the CFL2 accession/peptide entry in the supplementary protein list was not recovered. Preserve the source HDA assertion without inferring an extracellular mechanism from a general proteome description or treating intracellular function as disproof.

quote_policy: Authored primary quotations occur in YAML and the dated notes append, counted including repeats with a maximum of 25 words per source. Prior notes are preserved exactly and the whole current YAML/notes aggregate is also reported. Literal machine records and ontology definitions remain evidence, not new primary-paper prose.

followup_4562.binding_scope: Six class-specific binding refinements are supported by actual positive pairs and verified partner classes, outside the core; no partner catalytic or regulatory activity is assigned to CFL2.
